scope: Theorem 6.1 (Quantitative Leibman theorem, corrected box form) of the manuscript “Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers” (preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 164 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ab835f6a98c10d6d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a rational filtered nilmanifold as above, a number d of variables, and 0 < δ < 1. There is a constant A, depending only on these data, with the following property. If P : Zd → G is polynomial for this filtration and (P(v)Γ)v∈{0,...,N−1}d is not δ-equidistributed, then there is a nonzero horizontal character ξ of size at most A such that, on writing ξ(P(v)) = ∑︂ I αI (︄ v I )︄ , (︄ v I )︄ = d ∏︂ j=1 (︄ vj Ij )︄ , one has N|I| ∥αI∥R/Z ≤ A (|I| > 0). (6.1) Here δ-equidistribution means comparison with Haar probability to error at most δ against every observable of Lipschitz norm at most one. The constant A is independent of the coefficients of P and of N. The following consequence will be used. Fix also c, C, B, η > 0. Let Q ⊆ [−CZ, CZ]d be an axis-parallel box with each side at least cZ, sampled at its integer points. If |Ex∈Q∩Zd F(P(x)Γ) − ∫︂ G/Γ F| ≥ η, ∥F∥Lip ≤ B, (6.2) then, for sufficiently large Z, there is a nonzero horizontal character in a fixed finite list such that, writing ξ(P(x)) = ∑︁ I θIxI in ordinary monomials, ∥θI∥R/Z ≤ A′ Z−|I| (|I| > 0). (6.3) The list and A′ depend only on the fixed filtered nilmanifold, d, c, C, B, η. The same assertions hold with the nilmanifold and its filtration chosen from a fixed finite list.
